Card

Cards are flexible, extensible content containers. They include options for headers and footers, image placement, contextual border colors, hover interactions, and powerful display options.

Basic Card

The default card has a surface background, a subtle border and shadow, and a padded body.

Card with Header and Footer

Use .zak-card-header and .zak-card-footer to add extra structure. Headers may contain titles and actions; footers typically hold buttons.

Project settings Active

Configure project-wide preferences that apply to every member of the workspace.

HTML
<div class="zak-card">
  <div class="zak-card-header">
    <span class="zak-card-title">Project settings</span>
    <span class="zak-badge zak-badge-primary">Active</span>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-card-body">
    <p class="zak-card-text">Configure project-wide preferences...</p>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-card-footer">
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn-outline-secondary zak-btn-sm">Cancel</button>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn-primary zak-btn-sm">Save changes</button>
  </div>
</div>

CSS Classes Reference

Class Description
.zak-cardBase card container
.zak-card-bodyPadded body content area
.zak-card-headerTop header with flex alignment
.zak-card-footerBottom footer with right-aligned actions
.zak-card-titleCard heading style
.zak-card-subtitleMuted subtitle style
.zak-card-textBody copy style
.zak-card-imgResponsive cover image
.zak-card-img-topRounds the top corners of an image
.zak-card-img-bottomRounds the bottom corners of an image
.zak-card-hoverableRaises card and deepens shadow on hover
.zak-card-flatRemoves shadow
.zak-card-borderedEmphasizes border, removes shadow
.zak-border-primary / -success / -dangerContextual border colors

Accessibility

  • Use the appropriate heading level (h1–h6) for .zak-card-title, never skip levels.
  • Provide descriptive alt text on .zak-card-img images; use alt="" for purely decorative images.
  • When the entire card is clickable, use a single link or button wrapping the card, not multiple nested interactive elements.
  • Color borders indicating meaning must always be paired with a text label — never rely on color alone.
  • Cards inside a grid should remain keyboard-navigable and include visible focus states on any interactive controls.
